description: New Zealand geography, Latin phrases, military aviation, geology, British food, volcanoes, folklore, literature, flight systems, urban history and engineering make this one of the revival’s widest-ranging stretches of general knowledge.

s06e01.description: Cook Strait places New Zealand geography squarely in the question ladder. Islands, waterways and general knowledge combine in an episode where knowing roughly where something is located proves less useful than knowing exactly what separates what.

s06e02.description: ‘Annus horribilis’ gives the episode a magnificent Latin phrase for a terrible year. Language and history mingle with the wider ladder, and two words manage to sound both scholarly and brutally efficient, an achievement most metadata can only envy.

s06e03.description: The B-52 Stratofortress lends the episode eight engines’ worth of Cold War presence. Aviation and military technology provide the standout machinery while the question set ranges elsewhere with considerably less predictable flight planning.

s06e04.description: Hoodoos give geology one of its stranger and more memorable words. The sculpted rock formations anchor an episode full of mixed trivia, demonstrating that Earth itself occasionally names things as though preparing material for a quiz show.

s06e05.description: Melton Mowbray turns a Leicestershire place-name into a distinctly edible piece of British knowledge. Geography, food and culture intersect before the ladder moves on, leaving everyone suddenly aware that regional specialities are dangerous quiz territory.

s06e06.description: Mount Tambora brings volcanic history on a truly enormous scale. Geography and natural science give the episode its explosive centre while the surrounding questions prove that intellectual eruptions can occur without any assistance from magma.

s06e07.description: The Grim Reaper stalks into an otherwise civilised general-knowledge quiz and immediately improves the iconography. Folklore and culture share the ladder with more ordinary subjects, making mortality briefly just another four-option problem.

s06e08.description: Mario Puzo brings literary and cinematic crime history into the question set. A famous name sits amid broader trivia, with the episode testing the usual uncomfortable boundary between ‘I know exactly who that is’ and ‘I know one fact about him’.

s06e09.description: A four-digit transponder code gives aviation terminology its wonderfully specific moment in the hot seat. The episode ranges through familiar and obscure knowledge while one compact sequence of numbers proves that even routine cockpit systems can become trivia.

s06e10.description: The Spitfire gives the episode an unmistakable silhouette and a dose of aviation history. The ladder moves through other subjects, but few quiz answers arrive with quite so much cultural recognition packed into a single word.

s06e11.description: The iceberg theory turns what lies beneath the surface into the episode’s central idea. Literature and interpretation join a broad question set, fittingly reminding contestants that the visible wording is not always the whole problem.

s06e12.description: Kowloon Walled City supplies one of the catalogue’s most evocative place-names. Urban history and geography enter the ladder through a settlement famous for density and complexity, qualities the question set seems perfectly happy to imitate.

s06e13.description: The Aswan High Dam gives the episode monumental engineering on the Nile. Geography, infrastructure and history intersect in a ladder that keeps proving large human achievements are much easier to admire than to recall under four-answer pressure.
